title: Model router
evidenceStatus: 20 unique authored tasks across seven handlers, 20 correct after one recovered transport failure; original coverage 19/20. Exact request logs and actual UI callbacks inspected offline. No downstream execution study.
summary: The saved run agrees with all twenty simple authored route labels, but live requests use a different prompt and descriptions. An old response can replace a newly selected example, and arbitrary inputs have no clarification or unsupported route. Outcome receipts and held-out capability tests are needed before evaluating cheapest-capable routing.
strengths: Targets are withheld from model state and the choice schema is closed.
Published recovery preserves the original failure and request hash; original and recovered availability remain inspectable.
The UI explicitly limits its claim to handler selection and retains route probabilities.

findings.title: Recorded and live routing protocols differ
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:49; experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:29, :254. Exact recorded wire body asks for cheapest capable routing and resistance to embedded instructions; live prompt and all seven descriptions differ.
findings.impact: Saved results do not validate the visitor's current protocol.
findings.fix: Use a shared versioned builder/catalog and preserve exact prompt/criteria/hash for every run; test injection resistance explicitly.

findings.title: Late completion replaces the selected example
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:261, :430, :441. probes/routing.json starts calculator example 0, selects classification example 3, then installs calculator while input/dropdown stay on example 3.
findings.impact: The active example and displayed result diverge. The old result still contains its own text, so this is a selection inconsistency, not false stored provenance.
findings.fix: Guard responses by request generation, task hash, catalog version and active example; separate historical results from the edited draft.

findings.title: Missing context and unsupported work are forced into a handler
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:29, :210. No ask/none/unsupported option or availability state exists; the actual callback submits empty input with seven choices.
findings.impact: The live interface cannot express that no handler is capable or that a required document/page is missing.
findings.fix: Validate blank input, filter by explicit capabilities and availability, and define clarification/unsupported and multi-intent policy.

findings.title: Twenty lexical fixtures do not establish capability or routing savings
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:8. Two calculator cases and three per other handler; post-inspection seven-route keyword rules match 20/20. No handler prices, executions or outcome validators are used.
findings.impact: Label agreement is distinct from cheapest successful execution and calibrated abstention.
findings.fix: Freeze baselines before held-out task families, allow multiple admissible routes where appropriate, and measure downstream success/cost only with actual outcome receipts.

simulation.title: A dispatch desk with visible receipts
simulation.description: Edit a request, handler availability and required context; inspect the chosen route, run a bounded handler or a labeled recorded execution, and compare outcome/cost under one changed condition.
simulation.jevsRole: Interpret the request and select among explicitly eligible handlers or a clarification option.
simulation.codeRole: Own capability filtering, validation, execution adapters, permissions, state transitions, exact receipts and accounting.
acceptanceCriteria: Blank requests trigger no calls and unavailable handlers never execute.
Late answers cannot replace the active request or dispatch a stale action.
Selected route, attempted handler and validated outcome stay distinct.
Every receipt carries task/catalog versions and failure/fallback history.
Ambiguous requests use an admissible set or a defined clarification.

evaluation.design: Author 360 independent task families; reserve 90 development and 270 held out (30 clear per seven routes, 30 ambiguous and 30 unsupported). Two annotators label capabilities/admissible routes under explicit contracts. Three context/availability states and three unchanged passes yield 2,430 routing judgments; 270 paired embedded-instruction variants bring the total to 2,700 logical requests before optional batching. Split paraphrase families together, freeze protocols/thresholds/baselines and preserve wrong answers. Bootstrap paired metrics by 270 source families. Measure actual eligible-handler outcomes on a declared runnable subset before reporting cost regret, with a separately budgeted execution matrix. Exercise 1,000 offline asynchronous schedules across 100 seeds, requiring zero stale dispatches. Proposed runs remain unperformed.
baselines: Oracle from independently validated eligible-handler outcomes on a runnable subset.
metrics: Completed/attempted coverage, retries and routing latency.
Where measured: downstream success, invalid dispatches, end-to-end cost/time and regret.

coverage.current: 20 unique short tasks, seven classes, 20/20 final labels; 19/20 original completion plus one recovered navigation case.
coverage.full: Proposed 270 held-out families, 2,700 routing judgments and 1,000 offline integrity schedules; downstream execution is a separate declared matrix.
coverage.feasibility: No external benchmark score claimed. Needs richer fixtures, independent labels, protocol alignment and later provider budget; downstream costs cannot be inferred from the current cumulative budget snapshot.
